'''''Phoenix reclinata''''' (''reclinata'' - Latin, reclining), the '''wild date palm''' or '''Senegal date palm''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN |access-date=3 July 2024}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Arecaceae|palm]] family native to tropical Africa, the [[Arabian Peninsula]] and [[Madagascar]]. It is introduced in [[Florida]], [[Puerto Rico]], [[Bermuda]], [[Trinidad and Tobago]], the [[Leeward Islands]], [[Tunisia]] and [[Vietnam]].<ref name=POWO/> The plants are found from sea level to 3000 m, in rain forest clearings, monsoonal forests and rocky mountainsides.

==Description==
[[File:Reclinatabloom.JPG|thumb|left|Male inflorescence]]
[[File:Phoenix reclinata MHNT.BOT.2024.31.26.jpg|thumb|left|''Phoenix reclinata'' [[MHNT]]]]
''Phoenix reclinata'' is a [[dioecious]] clumping palm, producing multiple stems from {{Convert abbreviated|7.5 to 15|m}} in height and {{Convert abbreviated|30|cm}} in width. [[Foliage]] is [[pinnate]] and recurved, growing {{Convert abbreviated|2.5 to 4.5|m|ft|sigfig=2}} in length and {{Convert abbreviated|0.75|m}} in width. Leaf color is bright to deep green on 30 cm [[petiole (botany)|petioles]] with long, sharp spines at the base, with 20 to 40 leaves per crown.

The plants are unisexual and florets appear at the top of the palm stem. Male florets are a dirty, pale yellow and fall off after blooming; females are small, globose and yellow-green.<ref name = "Roodt (1992)">Roodt, Veronica (1992). ''Phoenix reclinata'' in ''The Shell Field Guide to the Common Trees of the Okavango Delta and Moremi Game Reserve''. Gaborone, Botswana: [[Royal Dutch Shell|Shell Oil Botswana]]</ref> This species grows edible, oblong [[fruit]], orange in color (when ripe), at {{Convert abbreviated|2.5|cm|sigfig=1}} in diameter. The fruit are borne in large, pendant clusters and contain one seed each.<ref name = "Roodt (1992)"/>

Palms across the genus [[Phoenix (plant)|''Phoenix'']] readily hybridize with one another resulting in naturally occurring variations.  They usually tolerate salt-spray, and moderate drought where the [[water table]] is permanently high.<ref name = "Roodt (1992)"/>

==Uses==
[[File:Phoenixreclinatafruit.JPG|thumb|right|Ripening fruit on ''P. reclinata'']]
In addition to the fruit, which attracts animals, including humans, the [[heart of palm|palm heart]] can be eaten as a vegetable. In [[Geography of South Africa#KwaZulu-Natal|KwaZulu-Natal]], and the [[Okavango Delta]], Botswana, the sap is tapped shortly before flowering to make [[palm wine]]. The fibres of young, unopened leaves can be used to make carpets, kilts and brooms. The roots contain [[tannin]] and can be used to make a brown dye. They also produce an edible gum. The wood is lightweight and not particularly useful.<ref  name = "Roodt (1992)"/>
